title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval (Lumen Health)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review quality eval results for the Lumen Health pilot. Discussed prompt set performance, scoring rubric anomalies, recent regressions on clinical note summarization, and guardrail tuning. Security and data residency questions surfaced; agreed to run targeted benchmark with updated prompts and submit security docs. Action items assigned for prompt updates, scoring spreadsheet share, and a benchmarking run next week.
next_steps: Redwood to send updated prompt set and eval harness by 2026-03-29
Customer to run privacy review for sample logs and provide feedback by 2026-04-02
Schedule model benchmarking (latency + quality) on Dedicated nodes week of 2026-04-06
SE to share scoring spreadsheet and threshold definitions (today)
Set follow-up sync after benchmark results: 2026-04-08 09:00 PT
action_items: Avery Chen: share updated prompt set + annotated examples by 2026-03-29
Samir Patel: run regression tests on quantized variant and share results by 2026-04-01
Evan Ross (Lumen): circulate privacy checklist to security team by 2026-04-02
Priya Kumar (Lumen): confirm SSO/SAML requirements and any additional audit log retention constraints by 2026-04-02
transcript:
[09:23] Avery Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining. quick checkin for the poc quality eval for Lumen. we have Samir from eng and jordan from CS. Maya, Evan, Priya, Tom from Lumen, thanks. how's everyone doing
[09:24] Dr. Maya Singh: good thanks. busy week but excited to see the results. we ran the sample batch last night and saw some odd summarization behavior on discharge notes where some medication names were dropped
[09:25] Evan Ross: yes i pulled the scoring spreadsheet, overall exact-match is okay but the clinical accuracy score dipped ~6% against our golden set on the latest model variant
[09:26] Samir Patel: got it. quick context - we rolled the quantized 4-bit variant to reduce token cost. that variant sometimes trades off recall on rare entities (drug names, dosages) due to tokenizer edge cases and kv-cache interactions. that might explain dropped meds
[09:27] Priya Kumar: this is a security question first - are any PHI samples leaving our VPC in the hosted flow? we only ran safe subsampled logs but want to confirm data residency.
[09:27] Jordan Alvarez: short answer is for hosted API we do see logs in Redwood's control plane for debugging unless you opt into private deployment; for the POC we've been running in Redwood hosted sandbox, logs are retained per the trial policy. Avery can share the security doc.
[09:28] Avery Chen: yes i'll share the SOC2/ISO docs and the sso/saml notes. also note we can move the evaluation to a Dedicated node or Private (VPC) if you need zero control-plane persistence, and we can enable KMS with customer-managed keys.
[09:29] Dr. Maya Singh: good - we'll review that. on the quality front can you walk through the scoring rubric, because the spreadsheet has a few columns we didn't expect (fluency, clinical accuracy, hallucination score) and we want to ensure alignment
[09:30] Samir Patel: absolutely. so current rubric: fluency (0-5), clinical accuracy (0-5), hallucination flag (binary but we track severity 0-3), and an overall accept/reject threshold. we've been using a micro-averaged F1 for entity overlap as well. i realize the entity match logic uses a fuzzy-match with token overlap so it can undercount when abbreviations differ (e.g., metformin vs met form)
[09:31] Evan Ross: that fuzzy matching caused a few false negatives in our golden set because of punctuation differences; can we adjust to normalizing punctuation and common clinical abbreviations?
[09:32] Samir Patel: yes we can update the eval harness to include normalization rules - i'll add a preprocessor to expand/normalize common meds and units. i'll also add a mapping table for synonyms.
[09:33] Tom Hale: any chance that the model variant is hallucinating diagnoses where none exist? we saw two notes where 'possible myocardial ischemia' was inserted when not present in original
[09:34] Samir Patel: that sounds like a guardrail issue - the model temperature and system prompt interplay can create over-confident expansions. we can tighten the system prompt to instruct conservative summarization and add rule-based post-filters to strip speculative language unless explicit in source.
[09:35] Dr. Maya Singh: what's the effect on latency and cost if we add those post-filters or change tokenization? we're sensitive to real-time constraints in triage workflows
[09:36] Samir Patel: post-filters are low-cost since they're rule-based. changing to a larger, unconstrained model variant would increase latency. Dedicated nodes can give consistent latency SLOs; for hosted we recommend batching + prefix caching to reduce per-token cost - but that can add a few hundred ms depending on your pattern.
[09:37] Avery Chen: to add: Redwood Optimize recommends conservative batching windows for triage use cases; we've included suggestions in the scoring doc. also want to call out that KV cache behavior on long notes can cause token drift; when the cache fills, generation can degrade. Samir is running a kv-cache stress test on the quantized variant.
[09:38] Samir Patel: status: ran 2k note stress test overnight. quantized variant showed throughput improvements (30% lower token cost) but we saw higher hallucination rate on extremely long input (>6k tokens). i'm attaching a log excerpt in the sheet. it's likely due to our current attention optimization not merging some long-range tokens correctly on 4-bit kernels
[09:39] Priya Kumar: from security - if we move to Dedicated or Private, what's the model for audit logs? retention windows? can we set a custom retention policy and export to our SIEM?
[09:39] Jordan Alvarez: yes, Dedicated supports custom audit log retention and ingestion to customer SIEM via secure forwarding. Private deployment supports air-gapped options. we can include that in the security pack i send.
[09:40] Dr. Maya Singh: good. another quick ask: can we add guardrails that check for medication entity presence and fail closed if meds missing in summaries for certain templates?
[09:41] Samir Patel: yes - implement rule-based checks: if template indicates medication list in source and summary does not contain at least one med-entity then flag for manual review. that'll reduce automation but increase safety.
[09:42] Evan Ross: perfect. what about regression detection - how will we catch new degradations after prompt changes?
[09:42] Samir Patel: we run a nightly regression pass that compares key metrics on the golden set and triggers alerts if clinical accuracy drops >3% or hallucination score increases by >0.5. we'll add a prompt-version label and link diffs in the dashboard.
[09:43] Dr. Maya Singh: can we have a gating policy so a new prompt set must pass before being rolled to production? we want a canary and rollback plan
[09:44] Avery Chen: absolutely. Redwood Rollouts supports canary percentages and automatic rollback on metric regression. for the POC we can do a 10% canary on Dedicated and monitor the clinical accuracy metric for 24 hours before expanding.
[09:45] Tom Hale: timeline - we want to decide hosted vs dedicated by next week to lock procurement. any blockers?
[09:46] Priya Kumar: procurement needs final security checklist and confirmation on KMS customer-managed keys. also SSO details. once those docs are in we'll start procurement flow
[09:46] Avery Chen: i'll upload the security pack and confirm KMS options today. Samir will share scoring spreadsheet now. Samir - you can walk us through the key rows?
[09:47] Samir Patel: walking through spreadsheet: column A = example id, B = source note excerpt, C = expected summary, D = model output, E = fluency score, F = clinical accuracy, G = hallucination severity, H = pass/fail, I = comments. flagged 14 failures in the latest run; 9 are entity misses, 3 are hallucinations, 2 formatting issues.
[09:48] Evan Ross: can you tag the 9 entity misses with the normalized tokens so we can iterate quickly?
[09:48] Samir Patel: yes adding normalization and tagging now; i'll push updated sheet and add a comment thread per example.
[09:49] Avery Chen: next steps recap - we'll send updated prompt set and normalized eval harness; run targeted benchmark on Dedicated with the quantized and full-precision variants; security to review docs and confirm KMS/SSO; schedule follow up after benchmark. any other items?
[09:50] Dr. Maya Singh: one more - can you include examples of the post-filter rules so our clinical reviewers can confirm they don't over-strip content?
[09:50] Samir Patel: yes i'll include the rule pseudo-code and a before/after example set.
[09:51] Priya Kumar: also please include the audit log retention options and a sample ingestion config for our SIEM team.
[09:51] Jordan Alvarez: noted - will include in security pack.
[09:52] Avery Chen: great thanks all. i'll send the links and follow up notes. next sync 2026-04-08 09:00 PT. thanks everyone
[09:52] Dr. Maya Singh: thanks
[09:52] Evan Ross: thanks
[09:52] Samir Patel: bye
[09:52] (end)
